body: And while extinction is a useful measure of biodiversity loss, it is not the whole story. It doesn’t capture population reductions or species disappearing locally or regionally. While “only” 1 percent of species have gone extinct on our watch, the toll on biodiversity within each region may be much higher, and this may be what matters most. From the perspective of existential risk, what matters most about biodiversity loss is the loss of ecosystem services. These are services—such as purifying water and air, providing energy and resources, or improving our soil—that plants and animals currently provide for us, but we may find costly or impossible to do ourselves.
